**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 1:**

(p-164) Surat al-Mursalat, also called al-'Urf.

Its purpose is to indicate the final destiny of humankind: the reward of the grateful with bliss, and the punishment of the disbelievers with the Blazing Fire, on the Day of Decision, after the gathering of bodies and the revival of servants, after this present existence is folded up and the familiar world is transformed. This is by His, glorified be He, power to make plants grow, to create sustenance, to send down knowledge and to widen understanding, so as to give life to spirits and happiness to bodies, through hidden causes and visible and unseen means. It also indicates His power to develop humankind through the stages of the years, to deposit faith in the bodies that He is pleased with, and to bring about disbelief among the people of loss and ruin. All of this is shared in the methods of this Qur'an, which neither humankind nor the jinn could match, despite their numbers and the length of time, by bringing anything like one of its verses. Its name is al-Mursalat, and also al-'Urf. The indication of this is clear to one who reflects on the oaths and recalls the meanings of the speech they convey.

(Bismillah) In the name of God, to whom belongs complete power over what He wills. (al-Rahman) the Most Merciful, to whom belongs general bounty upon all His servants. (al-Rahim) the Especially Merciful, who has singled out the people of His good pleasure for the completion of that bounty, and with Him is more.

* *

When Surat al-Insan was concluded with the promise to His friends and the threat to His enemies, and the disbelievers were denying this, He opened this surah with an oath affirming that it will indeed occur. So He said: ﴿By those sent forth﴾, that is, from the winds and the angels, ﴿in succession﴾, that is, for the purpose of bringing what is good from the Qur'an and the Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition) and other forms of goodness, and for bringing down the spirit and blessing, and for facilitating matters in regard to sustenance and other things. Or it means they come in a state of being successive and numerous, one following another. This derives from the saying of the Arabs: "The people came to so-and-so as one 'urf," when they turned towards him in large numbers. It is also said: "They came as one 'urf, and they were upon him like the 'urf of the hyena," when they gathered together against him.

Since the blowing of the winds is followed by the (violent) gusts, he joins with "fa-" (then), indicating sequence and causation, and says: ﴿And those (winds) that are violently strong﴾, i.e., the intensely powerful winds, immediately after their blowing; and (the angels) immediately after their cleaving of the air, by reason of the greatness of their bodies and their strength for swift and complete speed, ﴿in a mighty blast﴾, i.e., a great (blast), by reason of the beneficial results it brings.

When the spreading of the winds over the clouds lags behind their blowing and is slow in stirring, and likewise the spreading of the angels' wings, as a strong bird does in its flight, he joined with the waw, which admits both simultaneity and succession with or without an interval, the phrase: ﴿And those that spread﴾, meaning, for the clouds and the wings, in a gentle manner through the air, and for the laws that spread justice among people, ﴿spreading﴾. If you review the beginning of Surat adh-Dhariyat, you will gain further insight into this.

(p-166) Since clouds gather after being stirred up from the surging of vapors, become dense, and then carry water, and since this is well known, it having already been mentioned in Surat adh-Dhariyat, Surat ar-Rum and elsewhere; then after carrying, the clouds are compressed until some of them press upon others, and there open up gaps from which the rain emerges. He omitted all of that and mentioned this, saying with the eloquent fa' (al-fa' al-fasihah): ﴿Then by those that separate, separating﴾, meaning: [they separate] the clouds, until the rain (al-wadq) comes forth from within them; and [they separate] the feathers (al-ajnihah); and [they separate] between truth and falsehood, and the grain and the date-stone, and other things besides that.

Since the clouds, following the separating (of truth from falsehood), release from themselves whatever is in those clouds of water, or snow, or hail, or thunderbolts, or other things that God wills, which stir remembrance of God, and so it must be, while the angels cast what is with them of the Spirit that gives life to hearts, he said, using the fa' of sequence and causation: ﴿And by those who cast down a reminder﴾. He applied the term "reminder" (dhikr) to it because it causes it, if it refers to what the clouds carry, or to what the angels carry; and it may be that what the angels carry is literally the remembrance of God. There is no doubt that both are a cause for the rectification of religion and of the world.

When he had mentioned these categories, he explained them with His saying: ﴿As an excuse or as a warning﴾. Both are in the accusative as circumstantial objects (ḥāl), and both are plurals: ʿudhr (plural) in the sense of al-maʿdhira (the excuse) or al-ʿādhir (the one making excuse), and nudhr (plural) in the sense of al-indhār (warning) or al-mundhir (the warner). That is, these [winds] are divided into: an "excuse," if they have cast down beneficial, wholesome, fertilizing rain that does no harm, after a drought, for it is as though it were an apology for that hardship; and if the angels have cast down glad tidings, it is clearly an "excuse," especially if it comes after a warning. And into "warnings," if they have cast down thunderbolts, or what is in their meaning, such as large hailstones and the like, and likewise the angels. All of them are a cause for remembering Allah: one of them is a cause for people to offer repentance as an apology, and one is a cause for the punishment of those who are heedless of gratitude and who meet that with sins, or who attribute it to the seasonal weather-phenomena (anwāʾ).

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 7:

When these oaths were complete, comprising great matters and alerting to the fact that their causes, from the winds and the waters, were present among the people while they were unaware of them, just as the Resurrection may be like that, exactly alike, [he said], mentioning what is sworn to and emphasizing it because of their denial: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾, that is, what is promised of punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and of the Hour's arrival, and of the glad tidings for the people of obedience. He framed it in the passive because it is the thing feared, not because of its being from a specific source, although it is well known that it is among what God promised through the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿is surely to occur﴾, that is, it will certainly happen and must come to pass, and its causes are ready with you, even if you do not see them, as with these things by which He swore and what is produced by them.

(p-168) Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: God, exalted is He, swore by the angels who are sent in succession, by the winds that are subjected to His command, by the rain and the angels who separate, by its water, between truth and falsehood, and by the angels who deliver the Remembrance (the revelation) to the prophets, as an excuse from God and a warning. God, exalted is He, swore by what He mentioned of His creatures to the truthfulness of what is promised in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blazing fire﴾ [al-Insan: 4], and the verses thereafter; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing﴾ [al-Insan: 10]; and His saying: ﴿And He will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk﴾ [al-Insan: 12], and the verses up to ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [al-Insan: 22]; and His saying: ﴿They leave behind them a heavy Day﴾ [al-Insan: 27]; and His saying: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and the wrongdoers He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ [al-Insan: 31]. Had only this promise and threat, with which the surah concludes, preceded, the opening of the other surah (al-Insan) would have corresponded to it in the strongest correspondence as an oath upon it. How much more so, when the surah ﴿Has there come upon man﴾ [al-Insan: 1] contains Hereafter-oriented promises and reports of recompense. So He, glorified and exalted, swore to the validity of the occurrence, and He is the Most High, the Truth, and His speech is truth. End.

When it was known that they would say, in mockery, "When will it be?", and its time was among the things God has kept to Himself knowledge of, because hiding it from everyone has a greater effect on souls and inspires more awe in minds, He made His statement a consequence of that, mentioning what minds cannot bear, so that awe would increase and fear would grow greater, expressing it with the particle of certainty: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾ (p-169), meaning, despite their multitude, ﴿obliterated﴾, that is, their light is extinguished by the easiest of matters, so they become level with the rest of the sky. Their obliteration indicates that the one who does it has utmost power. He repeated the adverbial expression to emphasize the meaning, for added intimidation, and so he said:
[i.e., despite] its greatness, ﴿and when the sky﴾ ﴿is split open﴾, meaning it is cleft apart, so it destroys the ceilings and the lamps that are in them, with the greatest ease.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 10:

﴿And when the mountains﴾ — that is, despite their solidity — ﴿are blown away﴾ — that is, they are carried off entirely swiftly, and the winds scatter them, so they become scattered dust (habaʾan munbaththan), and no trace of them remains. This is like how grain is winnowed (yunsafu al-habb), so the stability of the earth, which rests on the causes that are the firm mountains, passes away, because that abode is not an abode of causes.

When He mentioned the change of the heavens and the earth, He mentioned what brought it about, saying: ﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾. That is, those who warned people of that Day and whom they denied. ﴿Uqqitat﴾ means that it reached the one who has no power apart from Him, with the easiest matter, its appointed time, for which it was waiting. This is the time of the severing of all means, of bestowing mercy and reward upon the beloved, and of wrath and punishment upon the enemies, through their testimony after they are gathered before the nations, concerning what answer they had given. The verb governing ﴿idhā﴾ (when) is omitted to make the matter awesome, so that the soul may wander in it in every direction. Its implied sense may be: "What you were promised has come to pass, and you saw in this threat what cannot be borne and what minds cannot comprehend or describe." This is what His saying indicates, instructing what should be said: (p-١٧٠) that it is said: "He..."

"For what Day were they deferred?" That is, for what great Day. "Were deferred" means that their deferment was made to occur for it; the verb is in the passive form because the point intended is the certainty of the term, not who set it, and as a reminder that the one who sets it is known to be Allah, whom no one other than Him is able to do this. Then he answered this question with the words, substituting for the "For what Day" (in apposition).

For the Day of Decision (ﷺ)... wait, no honorific here. Translation:

﴿For the Day of Judgment-Separation﴾, meaning: the one which, whenever it is mentioned without qualification, is not understood except as referring to it, because nothing is left in it without the separation (fasl) taking place in it among all creation, of every great and small matter. Then he magnified and made it terrible by his saying:

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Decision is?﴾

Translation of the commentary:

﴿وما أدْراكَ﴾ means: "And what would make you know?" — that is, what would inform you, even if you strove to learn it? Then he increased its magnitude (tahwil) by his saying: ﴿What is the Day of Decision?﴾ — that is, it is a matter that deserves to be asked about and to be exalted. Everything that is exalted by something is greater than it, and none of creation is able to reach knowledge of it, because there is no likeness to it by which it could be measured.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 15:

When He had magnified the matter, He mentioned what will befall them of severity in a general way, saying: ﴿Woe﴾, that is, great destruction indeed, ﴿on that day﴾, that is, when it becomes the Day of Decision, ﴿to the deniers﴾, that is, of the Sent Ones (al-Mursalat), which informed of that Day and of other matters of God's command. Originally, al-Waylu (woe, a term of dire punishment) is a verbal noun in the accusative, its verb being implied, but it was shifted to the nominative to indicate the permanence of its meaning. This sentence has been repeated in accordance with the number of oaths, and what is mentioned here of what will occur on the Day of Decision, from the obliteration and what follows it, is nine things, and one more was added, so that each sentence corresponds to one of the things mentioned. The tenth is for emphasis, indicating that for them there is woe that does not end [just as the One does not end]. Moreover, had they all been for emphasizing the first, that would have been fitting, for whoever denies you regarding several things, it is part of eloquence that you establish it with one of them, then say to him when the proof is established, "Woe to you," then do the same regarding all that follows, and repeat that very same statement to him, as emphasis for it and confirmation of the occurrence of its meaning, indicating that the rage has reached its limit, and the wickedness and the cutting off of excuse have left no place for him to evade it or distance himself from it. This is common, well-known and permissible in the speech of the Arabs.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 16:

When He had sworn to the occurrence of the promise and the threat in an unrestricted manner, more general than whether it would be in this world or in the Hereafter, because He is capable of all that He wills, with oaths that indicated His power over it by a clear indication, He followed it with an indication more evident than them, namely what is witnessed of the destruction of the world of souls (al-'alam al-nafsi). So He said, [denouncing] those who deny it, denying them in light of what came from Him, glorified is He, concerning those who denied the Messengers and those who believed in them: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿the former peoples﴾, that is, destroying them with punishment and wrath because of their denial of the Messengers, upon them be prayers and peace, like the people of Noah and those after them, nation after nation and generation after generation, We left none of them behind.

And since the destruction of those in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, if it were not less than the destruction of the former peoples, would not exceed it, and the answer to this supposition is: "Yes, indeed, He has destroyed them," He said, conjoining with what the context guided to, guiding it clearly, making it as if it were stated explicitly, what its supposition is: "Yes, We destroyed them."

Translation:

﴿Then﴾ i.e., after Our destroying them. Since the verb is in the nominative (marfu'), we know it is not conjoined to "tuhlik" (so as to be in the subjunctive); rather, it is a statement of threat, its implied sense being: "We, if We will, ﴿shall follow them with the later ones﴾," i.e., those who are in your time among the disbelievers of the Arabs and others, because of their denial of you; or those who came close to that time, such as the People of the Rass (ar-Rass) and the People of the Elephant (al-Fil).

When He threatened those who confronted the Messengers with denial, He consoled them (the Messengers), so He consoled those among their followers whose ties with them were cut, despite the kindness that is due to be maintained with them. [So He said -] beginning a new statement, drawing attention to the attribute that necessitates that destruction: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like that destruction, ﴿We do to the criminals﴾, i.e., all those who do the deed of those who cut off what God commanded to be joined, and who are persistent in that severing. This establishes for us the power to gather them for the Day of Judgment (yawm al-fasl), just as We had the power to gather them at the time of their crime, and to distinguish, in destruction and deliverance, between the deniers and the believers among the nations. So there must be the bringing into being by Us of the Day of Judgment.

Woe on that day to the deniers, [those who denied] the tempestuous winds by which We destroyed those nations: at times through the overturning and the rain of stones, at other times through water, and at other times through the earthquake, [and at other times -] without any intermediary.

(p-173) When He had mentioned the destruction in that manner, which indicates complete power over resurrection and over what is promised after resurrection, He followed it with the proof from the origination of creation, which is more evident. So He said, affirming and rebuking those who oppose their knowledge of this by their deeds: ﴿Did We not create you﴾, that is, O you who deny, by Our greatness which no greatness can count, ﴿from a despised fluid﴾, that is, a base, contemptible drop (nutfah), and it is [from -] mahana (with a fatha), as in al-Qamus, where it says: "al-Maheen: the lowly, the weak, and the little."

﴿So We placed him﴾: that is, by virtue of Our majesty, through sending down that water into the womb, ﴿in a firm resting-place﴾: that is, protected from whatever would corrupt it, such as air and other things. And We extended that for the sake of the progression through the stages of creation and the cycling through the phases of the making.

"Until a predetermined term" (ila qadarin): that is, a measure of time that God, exalted is He, appointed for the birth [—] "known" (ma'lum): that is, known to Us, of nine months for the birth, or more or less than that, which no one other than Him knows.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 23:

When this was of great magnitude, He translated it and explained it, exalting it by His saying: ﴿So We determined it﴾, that is, by Our greatness over that, or We made it according to a known measure of provisions, term of life, states and deeds. ﴿And excellent are We as Determiners﴾: We are, absolutely, the best of those who determine that and other things, or the ones who determine within those measures, because of the perfection of Our greatness, such that We make that come about through the direct action of whomever We wish from it, by his own willing and choice. Perhaps the expression "with what" (bima), together with the greatness, indicates the plurality of the causes that He established in that, through the angels and others. And in it, together with that, is a trial for the servants, both the monotheist among them and the polytheist.

Woe on that Day to the deniers (﴿ويْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾), i.e., when that occurs. "The deniers" means those who deny the scatterers (al-nāshirāt) that scatter those souls and everything that is to be scattered, while they know Our power over what was mentioned and its determination, from Our originating their creation and other things that demonstrate the perfection of power, yet they deny the resurrection and do not measure it by its like.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 25:

When He had shown, by the beginning of creation, the perfection of His power, He followed it with the proof drawn from the ending of His command and its middle, and from the benefits He arranged within them. So He said: ﴿Have We not made﴾, that is, We render by what We have caused, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿the earth a receptacle﴾, that is, a vessel receptive to gathering what is placed within it [and gathering it together in it], as one who gathers and collects (kaftan: a term from the root k-f-t, meaning to gather, bring together and cover), and it is a name for that which gathers iron, for example, that is, is coated with silver, and gathers and collects, like ḍimām (a bundle) and jimāʿ (a gathering) for that which gathers and collects. Or it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) used as an adjective, or it is the plural of kāfitah, like ṣā'imah and ṣiyām, or the plural of kafat, which is the vessel. ﴿And had We willed, We would have made it [a place] for you to be raised up when you are placed in it, as it raises up plants﴾. ﴿And We shall make that when We will the resurrection.﴾

Since it is known that the object has been omitted, which is "for you," he showed a state that also indicates it, [so he said]: ﴿living﴾ [meaning] upon its back, in dwellings and elsewhere, ﴿and dead﴾, meaning (p-175) within its belly, in graves and elsewhere, as you were before the creation of Adam, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 27:

When he (Allah) had mentioned what He has hidden from the mountains of knowledge and dominion and others, He followed it with what He brings forth of lofty peaks, to inform that if the act were of nature (al-tabi'ah), the matter would not be thus, for no one brings forth these great mountains, with their greatness, firmness, weight, hardness and other kinds of magnificence, except the Chooser who acts by choice (al-fa'il al-mukhtar). Besides this, there is what He preserves on their heights of waters which make trees grow and cause springs and rivers to flow; indeed, most of the water that comes forth is from them, and likewise most of the benefits from minerals and others. He said: ﴿And We have placed﴾, i.e., by what We have of greatness, ﴿in it﴾, i.e., the earth, ﴿firm mountains﴾, which, were they not there, it would quake with its people. And among the wonders is that their anchors are from above them, unlike the anchors of ships, ﴿towering high﴾, i.e., they are, while being firm in themselves and holding fast others, very long and of great height, as if they had risen proudly above the rest of the earth and above whoever wishes to climb them. Its indefiniteness (in the Arabic) is for magnification.

Since among the wonders that break customary patterns is the gushing forth of water, whose nature is to sink (yaghur) and not to gush (yafur), because of its heaviness and fineness, which gave it the strength to flow deep down, and because it comes from one place on the earth rather than another, and because it comes from the mountains which are the foundation of the earth and generally from their rocks, this is a clear indication that the act belongs to the One, the Chooser, the Subduer (al-Qahhar), and not to natures. He said: ﴿And We have given you to drink﴾, i.e., We made for you, by what We have of greatness, a drink for your giving drink and for giving drink to what you wish to water of livestock, tillage and other things, ﴿sweet water﴾, from rivers, pools, springs, wells and others, ﴿sweet and palatable﴾, i.e., great, pure and agreeable; though it was fitting that it be salty and bitter, due to what the lands that hold it contain of such (salinity).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 28:

Since this contains a clear indication of His power over the resurrection and other things, He said: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ [i.e.] the Day when the Hour is established, so that judgment may take place among the servants. He presented it in the manner of what is established and not in dispute, indicating that none denies it after the evidences have become manifest except one who has no sound nature (maskah). ﴿To the deniers﴾, i.e. those who are most firmly rooted in denial, to the extent that they denied what We have of distinction in this regard, the distinction by which We differentiated between one land and another, so that We made some of them suitable for the separation of its water from it, while some are not suitable; and We made some of them receptive to mountains and some not receptive — and other wondrous distinctions.

When the signs of the Hour had become manifest to a degree beyond which there is no further increase, and He had pronounced woe upon the deniers once and emphasized it thrice, so that it was due of the addressee to believe but he did not believe, He commanded with what indicates anger. Exalted is He, instructing them with what will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection when woe descends upon them: ﴿Proceed﴾, i.e., O deniers, ﴿to that which you used to deny﴾, i.e., that which for you has become like an innate disposition, ﴿with which you were denying﴾ in nonexistence, and renewing that denial while persisting in it.

(p-177) Since the purpose was to increase their rebuke, reproach, and terrifying, He repeated the command, describing what they were ordered to head toward, and said: ﴿Proceed﴾. This is according to the reading of the majority (al-Jama'ah), while Ruways from Ya'qub reads it in the past tense (ṣīghat al-māḍī), to indicate their complete submission there and that nothing whatsoever prevents them from it. The clause is resumptive (isti'nāfiyyah), answering one who asks: what was their state at this dreadful command? ﴿To a shade﴾, that is, of the smoke of Jahannam, which was called "yahmum" when it was mentioned in the Event (al-Waqi'ah), ﴿having three branches﴾, which branch out from its trunk, as you see great smoke separating into tufts. The specificity of "three" is because denial of Allah, His books, and His messengers is threefold, so each one of them punishes them with a punishment by which they know, there, for which denial of these it is. Or because what veils from the lights of holiness is the senses, the imagination, and the estimative faculty (al-wahm). Or because the cause of it is the estimative power residing in the brain, the irascible faculty (al-ghadabiyyah) which is in the "eye of the heart," and the concupiscent faculty (al-shahwiyyah) which is in its left side. It was also said: a neck of fire emerges, consisting of three groups: fire, light, and smoke. The light stands over the believers, pure flame over the disbelievers, and smoke over the hypocrites; it remains thus until the completion of the reckoning. Al-Razi said: the branches are flame, sparks, and smoke.

Since what comes first to mind from "shade" is that in which one seeks rest and relief, they assumed that this was the case. So He removed this misconception from them by way of mockery, so that the punishment would be more severe. He said, describing "dhī" (the one with): ﴿Neither shady﴾, meaning, not shading them from the heat in any way whatsoever. And since what was negated of it, namely the abundance of shade which the intensive form (ṣīghat al-mubālagha) conveys, might still have some benefit, He said: ﴿nor does it avail against the blaze﴾, meaning, it does not avail in any measure of averting ﴿the flame﴾, meaning this kind of flame.

I'll translate this faithfully, following the instructions.

When he had explained that this shade is within the punishment, and it was known that smoke arises only from fire, he said, clarifying that if there were a shade there it would not avail: ﴿Indeed, it﴾, i.e., the Fire, which the context indicates, ﴿throws﴾, i.e., from the intensity of its blazing, ﴿sparks﴾, which are what fly off from fire when it flares up; its singular is shararah, and they are the thunderbolts of that abode. ﴿Like a palace﴾, i.e., every spark from it is as if it were a lofty palace in its size. It was also said: it refers to the thick trunks of trees; its singular is qasr, like jamr and jamrah. It is a collective noun of genus (ism jins jam'i) that is used only for a plural, so it encompasses both many and few plurals. Likewise, every noun that distinguishes between a singular and a plural formed with the taa' is not a plural, because it is not a sound plural, which is evident, nor a broken plural, because its patterns are well known and it is not among them; and it is not a genus noun, since it does not encompass what is less than a plurality. From the greatness of its sparks, the greatness of its embers is known.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 33:

When He likened it in its size, He likened it in its color, saying: ﴿As if it were yellow camels﴾. Jimālat is the plural of jimālah, which is the plural of jamal (camel), like ḥijārah and ḥajar (stones), to indicate, together with the intensification (takbīr) of it, its abundance, its succession, its intermingling, and the swiftness of its movement. Whoever reads it with a ḥarf of ḍamm on the jīm (jumālat), then according to him it is the plural of jumālah, which is the thick rope from the ropes of a ship. He likened it [to that] in its extension and its coiling. There is no contradiction, for the sparks of it are sometimes like this and [sometimes] like what has preceded. ﴿Yellow﴾ is the plural of aṣfar (yellow), for the well-known color. It was also said: what is meant by it is a blackness inclining toward yellowness, as are the colors of camels.

Since this is a fearsome matter, its declaration is: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾, meaning, when that occurs, ﴿to the deniers﴾, that is, those deeply rooted in denial of the sending down of the Reminder upon the prophets as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner.

This is the Nazm al-Durar of al-Biqa'i on surah 77, verse 35.

When the reading "inṭalaqū" with a fatḥa (on the ṭā') indicated their immediate compliance with the command, without their uttering a single word, he made this explicit by saying, indicating what they are in of abhorrence and anger: ﴿This is﴾, that is, the station, which is a part of the stations of that day, and it was called a "day" because of the completeness of its rulings. Therefore he said, informing about the subject (mubtada'): ﴿a day on which they will not speak﴾, that is, not with a single word, because of the severity of bewilderment and astonishment in some of the stations, while they will speak in others (p-180) — for it is a long day with various states, as Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said. Or [it means] they will not speak what would benefit them, because in the world they did not speak the tawhid that would have benefited them.

Since they are unable to do anything except by God's permission, and what distresses them is the absence of permission, al-Biqa'i has put the verb in the passive voice, [indicating] the absence of any helper for them or any relief coming to them: ﴿And they will not be permitted﴾, i.e., from the verb adhina (to permit), ﴿to speak﴾, i.e., at all. Since the intended meaning is that no permission is granted to them and no excuse is offered by them, without considering that it results from the absence of permission (lest it be understood that they have an excuse but did not state it because permission was lacking), he said, with the verb in the nominative as a conjunction to "yu'dhanu" (they are permitted): ﴿and they will not make excuses﴾. This indicates the negation of permission and the negation of excuse-making immediately following it, absolutely. Had he put it in the accusative (fa-ya'taridhu), it would indicate that the cause of their not making excuses is the absence of permission, which would undermine the meaning.

Since this matter is a terrible one, he expressed it by His saying: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ — that is, when this station is as it is — ﴿to the deniers﴾, meaning those deeply immersed in denial, by means of the report of the extinguishing of the stars. Their punishment was made to be their silence, which is the going of the light of humanity, so that it would be like the extinguishing they denied.

This is the commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 38:

When he (Allah) had mentioned their bewilderment and confusion, which are the sign of the pronouncement of judgment, and since the stations of that Day were each called "days" because the judgments are completed in each of its stations, and this distinguishes it from anything else, He said: ﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾, i.e., that whole day is the Day of Decision, i.e., between what the servants disputed concerning, of truth and falsehood, the high and the low. Then He resumed His saying: ﴿We have gathered you﴾, i.e., O you who deny this Community, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿and the former peoples﴾, i.e., those whose destruction We had previously decreed, and they were more numerous than you in number and greater in multitude, so that We may separate between the disputants, and cause the punishment to burn, and recompense with reward. There was among you one who would say: "I will suffice for ten of the angels of the Fire." Then he pointed to the severing of all means, and said, giving this as the cause:

"If you have a scheme" — that is, O deniers, in a manner that is firmly established in your very selves — ﴿kayd﴾ means resistance through some kind of trickery or force — ﴿so scheme against Me﴾. This is a rebuke to them for their scheming against Our believing friends (awliya') in this world, by means of the means with which He empowered them, and an admonition that whoever harms His friend has declared war upon Him, while they are in fact powerless.

Since they were too insignificant to answer this and too contemptible to be given time for speech, He said, describing their state after this speech, drawing attention to the fact that if they had understood, they would weep now over themselves, for there is no escape at that time: ﴿Woe on that day﴾, that is (p-182) when this speech is said to them, so that it becomes an increase in their punishment, ﴿to the deniers﴾, that is, those firmly rooted in denial [that the heaven will be split open], as they used to deny that He would judge between them after death.

Since what happens after the separation is that each one settles in his own abode, [and it was -] he began with the deniers, because the warning in the surah is greater, so he separated them from the believers and said: "Depart..." to its end. He followed their opposites, the saved group referred to at the end of al-Insan, with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾ [al-Insan: 31]. So he said, emphasizing, both because of the disbelievers' denial of that abode and so that the believers would be happier than them: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing﴾, meaning those who used to place between themselves and everything that angers God a shield against what pleases Him, because of their established standing in this attribute on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿are in shades﴾. These are in reality shades [not -] like what was mentioned earlier about the shade of smoke, and the highest or finest shade in this world does not resemble them except in name. And [upon -] it indicates that they are real shades by His saying: ﴿and springs﴾, because gardens and great trees come forth from them. Just as it indicated that the branching shade mentioned earlier was for mockery, through the attributes of the Fire mentioned after it, so these springs cool the inner being, and the shading trees grow, just as the blaze scorches the outer and inner being and destroys whatever trees and other things are near it, so that nothing remains and nothing is left.

(p-183) When he mentioned the springs, he followed them with what comes forth from them, saying, indicating that their entire life is pleasure: ﴿And fruits﴾. And since among the fruits of this world there is something inferior, he said, indicating that their entire life is pleasure and that there is nothing inferior there: ﴿of what they desire﴾, that is, the desire.

Since he understood from the expression "in" (فِي) that they are established in all of this in the manner of something contained within its container, he said, drawing attention to the fact that by "fruit" is meant all foods, and that he only expressed it this way to inform that every eating therein is a means of enjoyment, none of it for bringing about benefit other than pleasure or averting harm: ﴿Eat﴾, i.e., it being said to them: partake of all foods in the manner of relish and delight, not for preserving health, for that is already attained without them. ﴿And drink﴾, i.e., of all drinks likewise, for their springs are not of water alone but of every drink, whether of food or of drink. ﴿Wholesome﴾, there being in none of that any expectation of harm. And He increased their bliss by making it a recompense, so He said: ﴿for what you used to do﴾, i.e., by your natures with which I created you, ﴿[you] were doing﴾, i.e., in the world, of righteous deeds founded on the basis of knowledge, which brought about belief in Paradise, and so necessitated its entry, just as the denial of the criminals regarding the Fire necessitated their entry into it and their punishment therein, and their denial regarding Paradise necessitated their expulsion from it and their deprivation of its bliss, as a fitting recompense.

Al-Biqa'i's commentary (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 44:

Since it might be imagined that this (reward) is for particular people during a specific time, he said, informing with generality and emphasizing it as a refutation of one who denies it: ﴿Indeed We﴾, that is, with the greatness that is ours, ﴿thus﴾, that is, like this great reward, ﴿reward the doers of good﴾, that is, every one who was deeply rooted in the quality of goodness. We are not like the kings of this world, whom their (own) desires prevent from doing good to some of the good-doers among them, (even though) they see that some of the people of their realm deserve it as a reward, because of their (own) passions and the weakness of their kings.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 45:

Since this bliss is a torment [great -] for those who do not attain it, He said: ﴿Woe on that Day﴾, meaning [when -] this bliss belongs to the God-fearing, the good-doers, ﴿to the deniers﴾, meaning those who deny that the mountains will be blown away, so that the whole earth becomes level, soft, even, with no crookedness in it at all, fit for springs and trees and for spreading out in its expanses however its owner wishes and chooses.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 46:

When he mentioned the bliss of the people of Paradise, which does not end, because for them there is the utmost ability to enjoy it, and that (bliss) is deferred, and the deniers were in ease in the world, and His saying (p-185) the Exalted was preceded: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to occur﴾ [al-Tur: 7] ﴿there is none to repel it﴾ [al-Tur: 8]; and when misery befalls after bliss, the promise of bliss abrogates it (naskh) — even if it was great and long — (making it) little; he said, as a result (natijah) of the answer to the oath, contrary to what is said to the righteous, as consolation for them and as grief for the deniers, on the basis of what its estimation is: the deniers in this world are in gradual leading on (istidraj) and delusion, and the state of their condition in the outcome speaks to them, as a reproach and threat: ﴿Eat﴾, that is, O deniers in this world, ﴿and enjoy yourselves﴾, that is, likewise, with the like of carrion, for enjoyment (mata') is among its names, as has been mentioned more than once from the people of lexicography (ahl al-lughah). ﴿A little﴾, that is, even if its time is prolonged, it is nonetheless passing, with its duration being short in comparison with the duration of the Hereafter, and this does not affect the precious remainder except one of base aspiration. Al-Razi said, and some of them said: enjoying the world is among the acts of the disbelievers, striving for it is among the acts of the wrongdoers, reassurance in it is among the acts of the liars, dwelling in it within the limits of permission and taking from it according to need is among the acts of the common believers, and turning away from it is among the acts of the ascetics, while the people of reality are too lofty in rank for the love of the world, its hatred, its gathering, or its abandonment to affect them.

When He placed them in this vile station, and the estimation was: there must surely be the befalling of punishment upon you on the Day of Judgment, He gave the reason for that by His saying, emphasized because they deny their being described thus: ﴿Indeed, you are criminals﴾, that is, deeply immersed in cutting off everything God willed to be joined (p-186), so it is not permissible that you be treated as the good-doers; therefore this was the outcome of this.

Woe on that Day to the deniers ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ — that is, when you are punished for your crimes — to the deniers, meaning those who denied the arrival of the Messengers at their appointed time, the time they used to threaten the criminals with in this world. They denied them for the sake of enjoying this paltry, turbid life, and they exposed themselves to the everlasting, unceasing punishment.

When the implied sense was: "They, in the abode of action, when it was said to them, 'Believe,' did not believe," he connected to it His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾, that is, to these criminals, by whatever speaker it was said, ﴿Bow down﴾, that is, pray the prayer in which there is bowing (ruku'). He used the name of the bowing for the prayer, calling it by the name of one of its parts. He singled out this part because it is used for submission and obedience, because it is specific to the prayer of the Muslims, and because some of the Arabs turned away from the religion on account of it. One of them said, "I will not bow (lā ajbī), because in it, so he claimed, there is an exposure of the buttocks, which would be an insult." The same applies to prostration. In the Qamus, he said: "Jabā tajbi'atan: he placed his hands on his knees, or on the ground, or he threw himself down on his face. And the tajbi'ah is that one stands in the posture of bowing." ﴿They do not bow﴾, that is, they do not humble themselves and do not perform the prayer. For this reason their threat was [given]. In this there is an indication that [the] command is for obligation, so that one who abandons it deserves the punishment, and that the disbelievers are addressed with the furu' (the derivative rulings of the law, as distinct from the fundamental beliefs).

Woe on that Day to the deniers. (Ver. 49)

That is, when the Decision takes place, [woe is] to the deniers, meaning: [those who deny] that which has preceded in this sūrah, or some part of it, or other than it, of what the Messengers have brought.

This sentence has been repeated according to the number of the parts of the oath's introduction, or the parts of the response, so that each sentence of it is a threat upon denying one of [those -] parts. This tenth sentence serves as an emphasis for those nine, and as a completion of their count and meaning, and as an informing that woe is theirs perpetually without cessation, just as the one [unit] has no cessation to it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 77, verse 50:

When this made clear that for them there is perpetual woe, he mentioned that its cause is their not believing in the Qur'an, and that whoever does not believe in the Qur'an will never believe in anything. So he said, giving the cause from the meaning of the speech: ﴿Then in what statement﴾, i.e., what remembrance whose revelation is renewed upon the one sent with it at every time when need calls for it, ﴿after it﴾, i.e., after this Qur'an, which bears witness to itself about its being rightly attributed to God Most High, through what it possesses of eloquence (balaghah) in its constructions, both with respect to each sentence and with respect to the arrangement of sentences with one another, and through its reports of unseen matters, its directing toward lofty aims, its alerting to rulings, and other things from the seas of knowledge and the gardens of the arts. Thus God, by virtue of that, is the Witness that it is His speech. ﴿will they believe﴾, i.e., will they renew their faith through it, through everything the Prophet (ﷺ) brought, if they do not believe in this statement, which God witnesses to be His speech, by what it comprises after its inimitability (i'jaz) from clear proofs, noble and suitable meanings, arrangements agreeable to natural disposition, subtle delicacies that soften every heart, and glad tidings that excite every ear. Whoever does not believe in it will not believe in the statement of anyone else, for there is nothing that approaches it or comes near it. So how [could one] claim that something can rival it or match it? Such a statement is only made when hope of the admonished is nearly lost, and custom dictates that punishment and the infliction of severity then descend. So it is among the greatest kinds of threat. Thus its last part has returned upon its first part in warning the deniers, and its first part has fit its last part in disgracing the criminals. And God is the Guide to what is right.
